These assays concern cloned regulatory elements; they do not establish endogenous expression changes, a causal nucleotide, or chromatin contacts in patient cholangiocytes. The molecular-function annotation identifies the linked protein’s normal activity; it does not establish the functional effect of each human susceptibility allele.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of zebrafish pkd1l1 causes biliary defects that have implications for biliary atresia splenic malformation.
evidence.snippet: These data highlight the essential role of pkd1l1 in normal development and function of the zebrafish biliary system, supporting a role for this gene as a cause of BASM.

nodes.description: Mutants have laterality abnormalities, sparse intrahepatic biliary networks and impaired biliary transport; most retain a gallbladder.
Multiple small spleens, a defining feature of the biliary atresia splenic malformation (BASM) subtype, part of the laterality/heterotaxy phenotype.

nodes.description: Sustained inflammation activates portal fibroblasts and transdifferentiates hepatic stellate cells into a myofibroblast-like, matrix-secreting phenotype — the organ-specific mesenchymal activation step of the conserved fibrotic response in the biliary atresia portal tract.

evidence.reference_title: Biliary atresia: pathology, etiology and pathogenesis.
evidence.snippet: The transformation and proliferation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) from fat-storing cells to myofibroblasts in BA plays an important role in hepatic fibrogenesis. HSCs are responsible for increased extracellular matrix, which leads to progressive scarring

nodes.description: Fibrotic and cirrhotic remodeling increases resistance to portal flow, producing portal hypertension and its splenic, variceal and fluid-retention complications.

evidence.snippet: Biliary atresia (BA) is an obliterative condition of the biliary tract that presents with persistent jaundice and pale stools typically in the first few weeks of life.

nodes.description: Conditioned medium from infected macrophages stimulates neutrophil chemotaxis; CXCL2 depletion abolishes the measured response.

In zebrafish, extrahepatic cholangiocytes have a relatively oxidized glutathione state and are susceptible to biliatresone-induced redox stress. Glutathione depletion sensitizes biliary cells, whereas NAC supplementation or Nrf2 activation reduces injury. This is a toxin-model mechanism; intrinsic glutathione deficiency has not been established as a general initiating human defect.

nodes.description: Arf6 knockdown and EGFR inhibition produce sparse intrahepatic biliary networks and impaired bile transport in zebrafish, with arf6 mRNA rescue. The human noncoding association does not directly establish deficient ARF6 expression or this complete pathway in affected infants. The molecular-function annotation identifies the linked protein’s normal activity; it does not establish the functional effect of each human susceptibility allele.

nodes.description: Neonatal BALB/c infection with RRV produces age-dependent epithelial injury, inflammation and extrahepatic obstruction. Early and late infection have substantially different outcomes. This defined viral model tests selected injury mechanisms; it does not establish the cause or all subtypes of human disease.

nodes.description: T-bet loss preserves duct patency despite continued obstructive-cholangiopathy symptoms and unchanged mortality.

T-bet-dependent inflammatory and cytotoxic programs contribute to duct injury in the RRV mouse model. T-bet deletion reduces these programs and preserves duct patency in many mice, but cholestatic symptoms and mortality persist. Duct patency therefore does not establish complete disease rescue.

evidence.snippet: Even though the percentage of T-bet KO mice displaying symptoms of an obstructive cholangiopathy and overall mortality rate was not different compared to wild-type mice, the extrahepatic bile ducts of T-bet KO mice remained patent.
